deities: Radha and Krishna (Sri Sri Radha Vrindavanchandra)

history.summary: Pune's first ISKCON centre was founded in 1984 at Camp. As crowds grew, HH Gopal Krishna Goswami Maharaj acquired a 6-acre plot at Kondhwa in 1995 and the New Vedic Cultural Centre was built over seven years under HH Radhanath Swami at a cost of Rs 40 crore, funded by the Camp temple and devotees. Inaugurated on Nityananda Tryodshi (23-24 February 2013) by President Pranab Mukherjee, it is the largest temple in Pune. The complex has two temples: the main Radha Krishna temple in North Indian style (red stone and marble) and a Venkateswara (Balaji) temple in South Indian style, plus a Brahmachari ashram, Gita Bhavan and community buildings.

name: ISKCON NVCC Temple
town_description: The temple stands at Kondhwa Budruk (Tilekar Nagar) on the Katraj-Kondhwa bypass in southern Pune, ~12 km south of Pune Junction, set in greenery on a 6-acre campus.

travel.road: Katraj-Kondhwa Bypass, Kondhwa Budruk; autos, taxis and buses from across Pune; in-house Govindas restaurant and gift shop

visitor_information.best_time: October to March; Janmashtami is the grandest celebration
visitor_information.opening_hours: Approximately 4:30 AM to 9:00 PM daily (with a midday darshan break per some sources - verify). Mangal aarti in the early morning; kirtans throughout the day
